articles.title: Ted Schlein's Ballistic Ventures seeks $490M for new funds amid AI-driven cybersecurity boom | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Cybersecurity-focused Ballistic Ventures is seeking to raise $360 million for a new flagship fund and another $130 million for a separate investment vehicle.
articles.body_text: Ballistic Ventures, the cybersecurity-focused venture capital firm co-founded by former Kleiner Perkins partner Ted Schlein (pictured above, second from the right), is seeking to raise $490 million across two new funds, TechCrunch has learned through regulatory filings. The San Francisco-based VC firm filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission this week to raise $360 million for its third flagship fund, matching the size of its previous fund raised in 2024, and another $130 million for a separate vehicle called Ballistic Ventures Fund B. Neither fund had recorded any sales at the time of filing. The fundraising plans come as the growing use of artificial intelligence has raised concerns about more sophisticated cyberattacks. The rise of AI agents has also created new opportunities for cybersecurity startups and the venture capital firms backing them. Founded in late 2021, Ballistic Ventures’ founding team includes Schlein, former AT&T Cybersecurity president Barmak Meftah, and Roger Thornton, who co-founded security companies Fortify Software and AlienVault. The firm has backed companies, including Talon Cyber Security, acquired by Palo Alto Networks , and Pangea, bought by CrowdStrike , alongside startups such as Armadin , GetReal , Nudge Security, and Oligo Security. Ballistic’s ties to storied venture capital firm Kleiner Perkins, where Schlein spent more than two decades, help set it apart from rivals, a cybersecurity investor at another VC firm told TechCrunch. Its investment strategy, however, is similar to those of other cybersecurity-focused investors, including Forgepoint Capital and Ten Eleven Ventures, the person said. In 2022, Ballistic announced its $300 million debut fund and raised another $360 million for its second flagship fund two years later. It also raised about $130 million for a separate vehicle called Ballistic Ventures Fund A, per PitchBook data. The new Fund B is targeting a similar amount. U.S. cybersecurity startups raised $11.5 billion in 2025, the highest since 2022, a recent report by JPMorgan Chase said, citing PitchBook data. AI-enabled companies accounted for about 72% of U.S. cybersecurity venture deals through May this year, compared with 36% in 2019, the report said. Separately, Microsoft, in its annual Digital Defense Report released last month, warned that hackers are increasingly using AI for activities ranging from phishing and social engineering to malware development. The technology is allowing attackers to operate faster and at greater scale, even as many of their underlying techniques remain unchanged. Ballistic Ventures declined to comment on its fundraising plans. When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission . This doesn’t affect our editorial independence. articles.title: Hiding inside Palantir's skyrocketing quarter is a foreboding signal | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Palantir's U.S. commercial revenue surpassed U.S. government revenue for the first time ever.
articles.body_text: The data analysis company Palantir delivered such a huge third-quarter earnings report on Monday that its press release even bragged that the numbers were “crushing consensus expectations.” Yet retail investors were lukewarm on the company on Tuesday, with the stock trading slightly down. That’s because Palantir’s enterprise sales, its big growth area, showed signs of slowing. First, the good news for the company’s investors. Revenue grew 96% from a year earlier, and 20% from the previous quarter, to $2.31 billion, beating analysts’ expectations of $2.18 billion. It was the first time Palantir has topped $2 billion in a quarter. Palantir also reported adjusted earnings per share (profit per share, excluding certain one-time items) of 44 cents, compared with analysts’ expectations of 41 cents. The company even raised its revenue guidance, or forecast, for the full year. Normally, that alone would send a stock soaring. The clincher was that Palantir’s U.S. commercial revenue surpassed U.S. government revenue for the first time ever. The company reported $984 million in commercial contracts (up 148% from the year-ago quarter), versus $953 million in U.S. government revenue. The reason for all this love from enterprises? They are signing up for the company’s AI software that can run frontier models and custom-train open-weight models securely, without sharing any of their data and business processes with outside AI labs. Plus, Palantir has long offered what is today known as “forward-deployed” software engineering, in which its own engineers work directly with customers to customize the software. However, Palantir also revealed a less-than-rosy signal: Even as enterprises are moving faster than ever, they are often signing short-term trials. “What Ryan and I are seeing on the front line and commercial is this much quicker interaction, much quicker to deployment, shorter duration of the contract but then an ability to expand that contract dramatically,” CEO Alex Karp (pictured above) told Wall Street analysts on the quarterly earnings call. Palantir is experiencing one of the unique phenomena of AI in the enterprise right now. Corporations are willing to quickly try AI software, skipping the usual bureaucracy, but they are also more willing to cancel contracts. Karp used one off-color metaphor after another to describe how unconcerned he was about holding onto his enterprise business. “We’ve gone from being the most attractive person in the physics department to being the captain of the football team, kind of thing,” he said, describing the influx of prospective corporate customers flowing in. “Conversely, you know, once you go Palantir, you don’t go back, and that’s just how it is, and you see it in our numbers.” The numbers don’t yet confirm Palantir’s long-term success. While the company closed a hefty $1.46 billion of total contract value from U.S. enterprises in the quarter, that’s actually a decline from the record $2.13 billion in the previous quarter. That suggests slowing sales, at least in the most recent quarter. The next earnings will show whether Palantir has solidified its role as a rising U.S. enterprise AI provider. Historically, many enterprises sign their biggest tech purchases in the final quarter of the year. Karp and his team certainly sound confident. They increased guidance for U.S. commercial revenue to be “in excess of $3.559 billion, representing a growth rate of at least 143%.”

articles.title: Researchers warned of North Korean hacking tactics years before record $6.3B Binance heist | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Cybersecurity experts have long warned of the persistent and patient threat from North Korea's long-running hacks. The world's largest crypto exchange was still caught off-guard.
articles.body_text: Crypto giant Binance says North Korean hackers used fake social media profiles and the lure of a potential job offer as part of a months-long scheme aimed at tricking an employee into downloading malicious software onto their laptop. Researchers have repeatedly warned about long-running social engineering attacks that can go on for months. This latest attack allowed the hackers to patiently worm their way into Binance’s systems to steal a record $6.3 billion in crypto last week, the company has now confirmed. The hack, disclosed in an updated statement posted on X on Tuesday, prompted the world’s largest crypto exchange to suspend customer withdrawals across its network. The FBI and blockchain investigators have blamed North Korea for the heist. The country has been long accused of carrying out massive cryptocurrency thefts in recent years to fund its internationally sanctioned nuclear weapons program. In its latest statement, Binance said that North Korean hackers, posing as recruiters hiring for a job, contacted a software engineer who works on wallets at the company. Following two interviews with the purported company, the engineer was instructed to download an apparent coding assignment as part of the interview process. When opened, the assignment contained malicious code that compromised the engineer’s work-issued laptop. Binance said its security tools did not detect the malware. That foothold in Binance’s network allowed the hackers to access an internal tool capable of taking over the work computers of two other engineers on the wallet team. One of those engineers had unwittingly downloaded a tampered app containing password-stealing malware months earlier after searching for the software in search engine results. While Binance replaced that compromised engineer’s laptop, the hackers used the engineer’s stolen credentials to break into the computer of a third engineer, whose job allowed them access to systems capable of controlling billions of dollars in crypto. Binance said the attack “should not have happened,” and that it had improved its network security following the theft. The hack underscores an ongoing tactic in the North Korean regime’s repertoire of attacks targeting the crypto industry and high-net worth individuals. Researchers have warned for years that North Korean hackers pose as venture capitalists, investors, and recruiters using dossiers of stolen American identities to trick employees into granting access to their systems. These attacks are widely known across the crypto industry and have been the subject of repeated warnings from the U.S. government and cybersecurity giants in recent years. Some half of all intrusions at U.S. tech companies last year were attributed to North Koreans posing as remote IT workers and fake recruiters. By Binance’s own account, the company faced at least 57 suspected attacks from North Korea, which it said reflect the “persistent threat posed by state-sponsored actors targeting the cryptocurrency industry.” But how the hackers were able to convince the engineer into downloading malware given the highly publicized threat, and bypass security weaknesses in Binance’s own network, will likely be the focus of investigators’ attention. While the case exposes how North Korean hackers use social engineering, such as offers of employment, to trick employees into granting access to their systems, it’s ultimately the responsibility of the company to ensure its systems cannot run unauthorized or untrusted software that could cause a compromise.

articles.title: AI inference startup Fal doubles its valuation to $16B as demand surges | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The five-year-old startup raised a $1.3 billion round led by Bessemer.
articles.body_text: Fal , a San Francisco-based startup that hosts and runs AI video, image, and audio models, has raised $1.3 billion in its latest funding round led by Bessemer Venture Partners, with participation from Nvidia, Sound Ventures, and T. Rowe Price. The deal values Fal at $16 billion, double its $8 billion valuation in April, Bloomberg reported . The startup announced its Series E and F rounds at the same time, noting that a combined $1.65 billion was raised across both. (Sequoia led the earlier round.) The latest round (Series F) comes amid soaring demand for inference services, the process of running an AI model that’s already been trained to generate outputs, particularly from customers relying on open source models. Fal surpassed $800 million in annualized revenue earlier this year, Bloomberg’s report noted. Companies providing inference services, including Baseten, Fireworks AI, and Modal, have also been growing rapidly and raising large funding rounds at higher valuations . But their gross margins remain thin because of the high cost of buying or leasing compute, according to several people familiar with inference companies’ financials. Fal was co-founded in 2021 by Burkay Gur, a former Coinbase machine learning leader and Oracle engineer, and Gorkem Yurtseven, who was previously a developer at Amazon. articles.title: Reddit tests ads in search results as traffic declines and growth concerns mount | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The new ad placements could help Reddit squeeze more revenue from existing users as Google's AI search changes how people discover its content.
articles.body_text: Just days after warning investors about declining search traffic and a weaker-than-expected revenue forecast, Reddit is looking for more ways to make money from its existing users. On Tuesday, the company announced that it’s beginning to test ad placements in its search results pages, allowing advertisers to reach users as they search for products, recommendations, and other information on its platform. “Ads in search may appear based on a range of factors, including contextual relevance to a user’s search query,” Reddit shared in its announcement about the new ad placements. “This is an initial test with a select group of eligible advertisers. During this test, we will evaluate and understand how users respond to these ads so we can refine the experience for users and advertisers over time.” The company offered examples of what sort of ads might appear, suggesting that a search for “espresso station” might display ads for espresso machines, coffee, or mugs, while a search for “home office setup” could surface ads for things like monitors, desks, and office chairs. The ad test comes at a time when Reddit is reckoning with how AI has been changing the web’s landscape, and subsequently its reach. Despite beating Wall Street’s estimates for revenue and earnings per share, the company’s stock dropped after it reported its third-quarter results last week , with fourth-quarter guidance that predicted sales of $1 billion to $1.03 billion, below expectations of $1.05 billion. This was tied to Reddit’s declining search traffic referrals resulting from Google’s move to an AI-powered search experience. AI search now sends less traffic to publishers’ websites, as features like AI Mode provide answers directly on Google’s Search Result pages, reducing clicks to other websites. Reddit also said that its global daily active users were flat quarter-over-quarter in Q3, reaching 130.3 million, while U.S. daily active users dropped from 53.2 million in Q2 to 50.7 million in the quarter, and were down 2% year-over-year. The company noted that if the trend continues, daily active users could decline to a low double-digit percentage by the fourth quarter. This leaves the company needing to earn more revenue from its existing users, which is where these new ads come in. The ads could prove to be more valuable to Reddit after it makes its planned shift to a logged-in experience, which was also announced during earnings. The company said it will make the transition gradually, initially in markets outside the U.S. The decision to limit its content to logged-in users serves multiple purposes — it protects Reddit’s site from unauthorized AI scraping, and it increases its value to advertisers. Logged-in users are worth more to advertisers because they provide additional signals about their interests and behavior, allowing for better-targeted, more profitable ads. articles.title: CrowdStrike to shell out nearly $500M for 2 AI security startups as the market for securing agents takes off | TechCrunch
articles.summary: CrowdStrike said it will buy Fiddler AI, which makes AI agent observability software, and Dreadnode, which helps companies automate AI security testing.
articles.body_text: Cybersecurity giant CrowdStrike is buying two AI security companies that expand its products to more broadly monitor, test, and cover AI models and agents, as companies across industries start rolling out AI agents and models wholesale. CrowdStrike said it will buy Fiddler AI , which makes observability software for monitoring AI agents inside enterprises, and Dreadnode , which helps companies automate security testing specifically aimed at detecting flaws in AI models, apps, and agents before they are set live. The company is paying around $400 million for Fiddler AI, and about $95 million for Dreadnode, according to The Wall Street Journal . The deals are happening at a time of significant upheaval in the cybersecurity space, especially as companies’ policies and processes lag behind AI adoption within their walls. Teams and individual employees alike are experimenting with AI tools, automating workflows, vibe-coding custom apps, and deploying armies of AI agents to do their bidding, which is understandably causing headaches for security teams. CrowdStrike, whose products are used widely across enterprises and governments, is clearly trying to leverage its already significant heft and presence to capture a share of this quickly burgeoning market . It’s not alone, of course, as we’ve already seen several startups and cybersecurity vendors raising dozens of millions in funding to solve issues for companies, though most of these approaches are essentially based on the conviction that existing security software isn’t enough to monitor and control AI tools, connectors, or usage. The company has itself been building detection and response controls , dubbed Falcon Guardian, to help companies see and understand what agents are doing on their devices, and these acquisitions seem to further flesh out its offerings. Fiddler AI is going to be part of CrowdStrike’s Falcon platform as Falcon Observe, where it’ll ostensibly help the company’s clients evaluate agents before they’re deployed, understand their actions, and monitor what they do, and feed that information as telemetry into the broader platform. Dreadnode, meanwhile, will be integrated into the Falcon Guardian product , to which the startup’s software will feed its testing results as security policy recommendations. Founded in 2018, Fiddler AI has raised a total of about $99 million to date, according to PitchBook. Dreadnode, founded in 2023, has raised $14 million so far. articles.title: Anthropic is still grappling with the economics of compute | TechCrunch
articles.summary: At a moment when Anthropic's compute margins should be getting better, they’re getting worse.
articles.body_text: There’s a lot of mystery around the finances of major AI labs, and as Anthropic inches towards it IPO, we’re starting to get some answers. In particular, the company is finally disclosing more about the economics of compute, and how much of Anthropic’s skyrocketing revenue is being lost to compute costs. In a new filing on Monday , Anthropic released data that showed those margins on compute actually getting worse. The filing was an update to the S-1 released last week — but where that filing’s financial disclosures only covered through June 30 of this year, the new data extended to disclose results through an extra quarter, to September 30. Broadly, Anthropic had a good quarter: revenue reached $17 billion, up from $11.5 billion in the previous quarter, suggesting durable growth. But the operating loss grew at the same time, thanks in large part to growing compute costs. Looking at the compute margins makes the picture even worse. In the new quarter, compute took up 58% of the company’s revenue, up from 48% the quarter before. At a moment when the company could win over IPO investors by showing margins improving, they’re getting worse. A chart in the filing shows this even more clearly, tracking the company’s revenue for every dollar spent on compute. Since the start of 2025, it’s been steadily growing, peaking at just over 2x this past quarter, then falling back down to 1.72x. Many indications imply that this shift in compute margins is more of a blip than a long-term problem, but it still tells us important things about the business of running a major lab. Trying to keep up with demand, Anthropic’s compute bill shot up to $10 billion for the quarter, including, as the filing notes, “$5.0 billion of compute under short-term commitments, which currently costs significantly more than comparable compute procured under our multi-year commitments.” Basically, demand was growing so fast that Anthropic had to scramble for compute, which meant paying higher rates. Some of those deals have already played out in public. Anthropic has been paying SpaceX $1.25 billion a month for compute, alongside multibillion-dollar deals with Nscale , Akamai , and Volta . In the parlance of the industry, these are neoclouds rather than hyperscalers — smaller outfits that offer more flexible compute deals at higher rates. Anthropic’s margins got worse in Q3 because of deals like these, and there’s no sign they’ll be able to do without them anytime soon. As the new filing puts it, “We expect compute and infrastructure expenses to increase in absolute dollars and remain our largest operating expense for the foreseeable future as additional committed compute becomes available to us under multi-year arrangements with CSPs, and as we continue to invest in additional compute.” Anthropic is still trying to lower its compute costs. In particular, the company talks quite a bit about its efforts to build its own compute base under a project it calls “Anthropic Direct.” But with demand growing so fast, those efforts aren’t going to be able to keep pace, and the neoclouds will continue to be the best option they have. In a sense, these are champagne problems. As long as revenue is growing at nearly 50% a quarter, few investors will worry about high compute costs — and the moment demand slows down, investors may be comforted by a compute picture that has gotten a lot sunnier. But it’s a reminder of how much AI labs still depend on the trillion-dollar infrastructure buildout — and how vulnerable they are to hiccups in that process. It’s easy to imagine the data center buildout slowing down over the next year if bond markets get skittish or local opposition gets more intense. There’s not much Anthropic can do to address either of those risks, and either one would make a messy compute picture a whole lot messier. In the meantime, the future of Anthropic and other labs will be at the mercy of compute prices. When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission . articles.title: Chris Pappas första homosexuella senatorn i USA
articles.summary: Chris Pappas blir den första öppet homosexuella senatorn någonsin i USA.
articles.body_text: Chris Pappas blir den första öppet homosexuella senatorn någonsin i USA. – Jag tror att människor, oavsett politisk uppfattning, egentligen bara vill att deras grannar ska kunna vara sig själva, sade han till The New York Times i oktober. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Chris Pappas, från New Hampshire, vann valet mot den tidigare senatorn John E. Sununu. Han blir därmed den första öppet homosexuella senatorn någonsin. – Jag tror att människor, oavsett politisk uppfattning, egentligen bara vill att deras grannar ska kunna vara sig själva, sade Pappas till The New York Times i oktober. Själv har han inte ägnat någon tid under valkampanjen att poängtera att han skriver historia om han skulle bli invald i senaten. Inte heller har hans valrörelse ägnats åt att lyfta fram hbtqi-personers utsatthet. I stället har han, liksom många andra demokrater fokuserat sina tal på de ekonomiska försämringar som Donald Trumps andra mandatperiod inneburit för många amerikaner. Pappas kom ut som homosexuell under studentåren på Harvard och har i intervjuer pratat om sin rädsla tidigare i ungdomen för att vara öppen med sin sexualitet. Han har suttit fyra mandatperioder i representanthuset och är ordförande för Congressional Equality Caucus, en sammanslutning som arbetar för jämlikhet för hbtq-personer i kongressen. Han var med och introducerade lagförslaget som skyddar samkönade äktenskap på federal nivå. Lagen undertecknades av president Joe Biden i december 2022. Under sitt segertal kort efter att valresultatet stod klart, riktade han sig till sin make. – Tack till mannen som står bredvid mig, min otroliga make Vann. Chris Pappas efterträder senator Jeanne Shaheen. Detta är en nyhetsartikel. Expressen granskar, avslöjar och ger dig senaste nyheterna på ett sakligt sätt. Mer om oss här. Vill du tipsa oss om något? articles.title: Uppgifter: Ryssland ska utnyttja en försvagad Trump
articles.summary: Utgången i det amerikanska mellanårsvalet kan få stora konsekvenser för kriget i Ukraina. Enligt källor till Bloomberg kan en försvagad Trump förändra hela spelplanen inför fredsförhandlingarna.
articles.body_text: Utgången i det amerikanska mellanårsvalet kan få stora konsekvenser för kriget i Ukraina. Enligt källor till Bloomberg kan en försvagad Trump förändra hela spelplanen inför fredsförhandlingarna. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Utfallet i det amerikanska mellanårsvalet kommer inte bara påverka amerikansk mark. Enligt Bloomberg skulle det även kunna få stora konsekvenser för kriget i Ukraina. De har pratat med källor som säger att Kreml tappat tron på att USA:s president, Donald Trump, kan få Ukraina att gå med på ett fredsavtal, som är fördelaktigt för Ryssland . Bloomberg skriver även att en förlust i mellanårsvalet knappast kommer få Trump att vilja ge mer Ukrainastöd. Källorna säger vidare att det kan få Ryssland att trappa upp attackerna mot Ukraina – för att få dem att kapitulera. Men även att Kreml kan försöka förlänga kriget för att pressa europeiska länder att mana till fred. Detta kommer troligtvis dras till sin spets under fredssamtalen mellan Ryssland, Ukraina och USA senare i november då Ryssland kan testa en försvagad Trump vid förhandlingsbordet. Trump kan dock redan vara försvagad. Inför mellanårsvalet valde han att runda de ryska sanktionerna genom att köpa rysk diesel för att försöka få ner drivmedelspriset i USA. Nu säger den Kreml-nära källan till Bloomberg att landet vill leta efter nya sätt att kunna lätta på de amerikanska sanktionerna. ” Målet hade varit att övertala Trump att USA och Ryssland kan göra affärer tillsammans utan att först avsluta kriget i Ukraina ”, skriver de. Vissa öppningar verkar redan ha skett. Trumps svärson Jared Kushner och USA:s sändebud Steve Witkoff ska redan ha försökt övertala Putin med potentiella affärskontrakt som kan läggas på bordet när man nått fred, enligt New York Times. articles.title: Kände till bristerna – före Ica-attacken
articles.summary: Natten till måndagen höjdes temperaturen i flera matbutikers kyldiskar. Nu berättar företaget bakom systemen att säkerhetsbristerna var kända långt före angreppet. – Det här är lite av ett misslyckande, säger Fredrik Blix, doktor i cybersäkerhet, till SVT.
articles.body_text: Natten till måndagen höjdes temperaturen i flera matbutikers kyldiskar. Nu berättar företaget bakom systemen att säkerhetsbristerna var kända långt före angreppet. – Det här är lite av ett misslyckande, säger Fredrik Blix, doktor i cybersäkerhet, till SVT . Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Totalt 23 Ica -butiker och sju Coop-butiker drabbades under natten till måndagen av ett cyberangrepp när temperaturen i kyldiskarna höjdes, i vissa fall till så högt som 50 grader. Liknande incidenter har rapporterats i ett flertal europeiska länder. Nu berättar företaget bakom systemen, Danfoss, att de länge vetat att det funnits en risk för hackare att komma åt systemen – och att de påtalat det till sina kunder för flera månader sedan. I Frankrike inträffade en liknande attack som den i Sverige, den 12 oktober. Hackare kom åt kylarna genom föråldrad mjukvara. Misstanken är att det är det som skett även i Sverige. Danfoss hävdar att de har uppmärksammat butikerna på detta och länge rekommenderat dem att åtgärda bristerna, enligt The Guardian . Expressen har sökt Ica och ställt frågan om de informerat sina handlare om vikten att uppdatera mjukvaran som sköter kylarna, men inte fått något svar. På frågan om Ica varnat de svenska butikerna efter attacken i Frankrike svarar Gustaf Nilsson, pressansvarig på Ica, i ett mejl att de tar säkerheten på stort allvar. ”Vi tar som sagt driftsäkerhet på stort allvar och arbetar kontinuerligt med säkerheten i dialog med handlarna”. Fredrik Blix, doktor i cybersäkerhet, säger till SVT att attacken i Frankrike borde manat till eftertanke och kallar det hela för ett misslyckande.

articles.title: Trump hoppas – men befarar katastrof
articles.summary: Donald Trump hoppas på bra siffror i mellanårsvalet. Samtidigt befarar han ett katastrofval, enligt källor till CNN.
articles.body_text: Donald Trump hoppas på bra siffror i mellanårsvalet. Samtidigt befarar han ett katastrofval, enligt källor till CNN. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Amerikanarna går återigen till valurnorna. Det är två år sedan det senaste presidentvalet som Donald Trump gick segrande ur. Nu röstar medborgarna om alla platser i representanthuset och en tredjedel av platserna i senaten. I dagsläget sitter Republikanerna på makten i båda kamrarna. New York Times senaste opinionsmätning från måndagen visade en ökning för Demokraterna i senaten i sex av de sju delstater som kan avgöra valet. Bettingsajten Polymarket pekar på att det är 74 procents sannolikhet att Demokraterna kammar hem både senaten och representanthuset. Den amerikanska presidenten följer valresultatet för mellanårsvalet från East Room, festsalen i Vita huset , tillsammans med ett mindre sällskap bestående av hans närmaste medarbetare och rådgivare. Enligt källor till CNN har Donald Trump verkat hoppfull under valkampanjen, tänkt att de opinionsundersökningar som publicerats varit felaktiga och att Republikanerna skulle slå underifrån. Att partiet skulle lyckas betydligt bättre än det verkat. I samtal med sina medarbetare har han själv påstått att hans eget engagemang varit tillräckligt för att republikanerna ska kunna undvika ett katastrofval. I privata sammanhang har han däremot, enligt CNN:s källor, medgett att hans eget parti kan stå inför det sämsta möjliga scenariot – att Republikanerna förlorar både representanthuset och senaten ditt de blåa. articles.summary: Följ Expressens direktrapport med senaste nytt om valet.
articles.body_text: I Florida vinner den republikanska senatorskandidaten Ashley Moody, skriver flera medier. Delstaten är historiskt republikansk, och Moodys seger innebär att de behåller kvar sin plats. Andy Barr blir Kentuckys nya senator och ersätter därmed den tidigare majoritetsledaren Mitch McConnell och Kevin Hern utropas som segrare i Oklahoma. Båda resultaten är mycket väntade. Atlantas tidigare borgmästare Keisha Lance Bottoms utropas som segrare i guvernörsvalet i Georgia av NBC News . Därmed besegrar hon republikanen Rick Jackson och blir första demokraten på posten på 24 år. Hon blir också den första kvinnan och den första svarta personen på posten – och den första svarta kvinnan att bli guvernör i USA. Resultatet ger också delstatens senator Jon Ossoff möjlighet att ställa upp som presidentkandidat, som många demokrater önskar sig. Om han blir president kan han inte sitta kvar som senator – och den som utnämner ny senator då är guvernören. Det hade alltså blivit bekymmersamt om Jackson vunnit guvernörsvalet. I New Mexico blir demokraten Ben Ray Luján återvald som senator och i New York segrar demokraten Kathy Hochul igen. I den demokratiska delstaten Colorado segrar John Hickenlooper och får starta sin andra mandatperiod. I West Virginia och Wyoming segrar väntat två republikaner platsen i senaten, rapporterar flera medier. I West Virginia Shelley Moore Capito för att vara senator en tredje mandatperiod. I Wyoming vinner Harriet Hageman. Demokraten James Talarico leder senatsvalet i delstaten Texas, rapporterar flera medier. Valet i Texas har varit ett av de mest uppmärksammade under valrörelsen och Talarico har trätt fram som ett demokratiskt stjärnskott.

articles.body_text: Nu vid midnatt stänger de första vallokalerna i USA, i Indiana och Kentucky. Två röda – alltså republikanska – delstater.
